blocks.value: Data in a file is organized in layers: characters (single letters, numbers, or symbols) combine into fields (a meaningful group of characters), fields combine into records (all the data about one entity), and records combine into a file.
A file whose records are read in the order they were stored is called a sequential access file. Fields within a record are sometimes separated by commas, known as comma-separated values.
A stream is a flow of data. Data flowing from a source (a file, the keyboard) into a program is an input stream; data flowing from a program to a destination (a file, the screen) is an output stream.

A buffer is a memory location that temporarily holds data being read or written, making repeated reads and writes more efficient. Flushing forces any buffered data that hasn't been written out yet to actually be written.
